author: The Sconi
title: Manitowoc County Historical Society offers free admission for mothers on May 9
text:
The Manitowoc County Historical Society Museum and Pinecrest Village will offer free general admission for mothers on May 9, according to an announcement released on Apr. 29. The event will take place at the museum’s location at 924 Pinecrest Road in Manitowoc and will feature hands-on activities, demonstrations, and a special tea program.
The initiative is part of the museum’s celebration of Mother’s Day weekend. Interpreters in the Historic Village will demonstrate various tasks and activities that reflect life for mothers in the nineteenth century. Visitors can explore historic homes, kitchens, and heirloom gardens during the event hours from 10 a.m. to 4 p.m., with living history interpreters available from 10 a.m. to 1 p.m.
A Mother’s Day tea is scheduled for 1 p.m., where guests will enjoy afternoon tea accompanied by a program featuring a historical fashion show inspired by American Girls dolls. Participants are invited to bring their own dolls or stuffed animals. Tickets for the Mother’s Day Tea include general admission for the day, but advanced registration is required for all attendees who wish to participate in the tea.
For additional information about Mother’s Day Weekend events or registration details for the tea program, interested individuals are encouraged to contact the Manitowoc County Historical Society at (920) 684-4445 or visit ManitowocCountyHistory.org.
The Manitowoc County Historical Society Museum and Pinecrest Village is located in eastern Wisconsin’s Kettle Moraine countryside. The site features over sixty acres of interpretive exhibits including more than twenty-five historic buildings furnished with items representing early settlers of Manitowoc County.
